assignment.title: Algebra II Honors — Lesson 1 Day 2: Function Attributes and Relations

questions.prompt: Use the graph of f(x) = |x + 1| − 2. State the domain and range.
Graph −2 ≤ x < 4 and write the interval in interval notation.
Build the mapping for {(−2, 1), (0, 3), (2, 5)} and state the domain and range.
Use the graph of f(x) = (x − 2)² − 4. State where the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.
Use the graph of f(x) = −(x − 1)² + 4. State where the function is positive and where it is negative.
Use the graph of f(x) = |x + 2| − 3. State where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, and negative.
Represent {(−3, 2), (0, 5), (0, −1), (4, 2)} with a mapping and a coordinate plot. State the domain and range, then decide whether it is a function.
Complete the table for f(x) = 0.5x + 1 over x ∈ {−2, 0, 2, 4}, plot only those points, state the domain and range, and classify the relation as discrete or continuous.
Build a model for the money collected from selling chocolate bars.
questions.scenario: A student group sells chocolate bars for $2 each. The function M(x) gives the amount of money collected after selling x chocolate bars.
questions.domainPrompt: Choose the reasonable domain for the number of chocolate bars sold.
questions.rangePrompt: Choose the corresponding range for the money collected.

solutionReview.headline: The money collected depends on how many bars are sold, $2 for each, and only whole bars are sold.
reasoning: Input and output: the money collected depends on how many bars are sold, so the input is the number of chocolate bars sold and the output is the money collected in dollars.
Function: each bar brings in $2, so x bars bring in 2 times x dollars: M(x) = 2x.
Discrete or continuous: the group sells whole bars, never part of one, so the relationship is discrete.
Graph: plot the table’s points (0, 0), (1, 2), (2, 4) and (3, 6) as separate points, without connecting them.
Domain: the group can sell 0 bars, or 1, 2, 3 and so on, so the domain is {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.
Range: each number of bars brings in twice as many dollars, 0, 2, 4, 6 and so on, so the range is {0, 2, 4, 6, ...}.
solutionReview.answerSummary: M(x) = 2x; the relationship is discrete, with domain {0, 1, 2, 3, ...} and range {0, 2, 4, 6, ...}.

questions.prompt: Build a model for the water released by the shower head.
questions.scenario: A low-flow shower head releases 1.8 gallons of water per minute. Let t be time in minutes and let V(t) be the total gallons released.
questions.domainPrompt: State the reasonable domain for time in interval notation.
questions.rangePrompt: State the reasonable range for water volume in interval notation.

solutionReview.headline: The water released depends on the time, 1.8 gallons each minute, and time and water flow without jumps.
reasoning: Input and output: the water released depends on how long the shower runs, so the input is the time in minutes and the output is the water released in gallons.
Function: each minute releases 1.8 gallons, so t minutes release 1.8 times t gallons: V(t) = 1.8t.
Discrete or continuous: time passes through every value, not only whole minutes, and the water flows the whole time, so the relationship is continuous.
Graph: plot the table’s points (0, 0), (0.5, 0.9), (2.5, 4.5) and (5, 9), then draw one connected line through them, starting at (0, 0).
Domain: the time can be 0 minutes or any amount more, so the domain is [0, ∞).
Range: the water released starts at 0 gallons and keeps growing while the shower runs, so the range is [0, ∞).
solutionReview.answerSummary: V(t) = 1.8t; the relationship is continuous, with domain [0, ∞) and range [0, ∞).

Complete the table for f(x) = −x + 4 over x ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, plot the points, state the range, and classify the relation.
A taxi fare is modeled by C(t) = 3t + 5 for any real travel time t from 0 to 20 minutes. Complete the attributes.

optionRationales.discrete: Discrete fits separate counts, like whole trips; here t can be any real time, such as 2.5 minutes.
optionRationales.continuous: Travel time can be any real number from 0 to 20, so the graph is one unbroken segment.

optionRationales.[0, 20]: t can be any real time from 0 to 20 minutes, with both endpoints included.
optionRationales.{0, 1, 2, …, 20}: This lists whole minutes only, but the time can be any real number, like 7.5.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): The formula works for any t, but the situation only allows times from 0 to 20 minutes.

optionRationales.[5, 65]: The fare starts at C(0) = 5 and rises to C(20) = 65, taking every value between.
optionRationales.[0, 60]: This leaves out the + 5 in the fare: 3t alone runs from 0 to 60.
optionRationales.{5, 8, 11, …, 65}: This lists fares for whole minutes only, but t can be any real time, so the fares fill in between.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = −(x − 2)² + 9, state the intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, and negative.
Represent {(−1, 2), (2, 5), (2, −3), (6, 1)} with a mapping. State the domain and range and decide whether it is a function.
A tank is filled at 4 gallons per minute for exactly 12 minutes. Let V(t)=4t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 12. Complete the attributes.

optionRationales.discrete: Discrete fits separate counts; here time runs through every value, including parts of a minute.
optionRationales.continuous: Water flows in at every moment, so t takes every real value from 0 to 12 and the graph is unbroken.

optionRationales.[0, 12]: The rule holds for 0 ≤ t ≤ 12: every real time, with both endpoints included.
optionRationales.{0, 1, 2, …, 12}: This keeps whole minutes only, but t can be any real time, like 3.5 minutes.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): The formula works for any t, but the filling only lasts from 0 to 12 minutes.

optionRationales.[0, 48]: The volume starts at V(0) = 0 and reaches V(12) = 48, taking every value between.
optionRationales.[4, 48]: This starts the volume at the rate, 4 gallons, instead of at the volume when t = 0.
optionRationales.{0, 4, 8, …, 48}: This lists volumes at whole minutes only, but time runs continuously, so the volume fills in between.
